From Effective Altruism to Collective Altruism

Intelligence has real costs. We must always ask what it is for, who benefits, who bears the costs, and who decides.

1. Intelligence has a physical cost

AI work happens in the cloud, but its costs are grounded in the real world.

AI Computation
tokens · models · inference
Data Centers
hyperscalers · neoclouds · chips
Real Inputs
electricity · water · land
minerals · labor
Real Impacts
communities · ecosystems · workers

2. Two different economic logics

The issue is not only how much intelligence we can produce, but what it is used for and how value circulates.

Artificial Intelligence
Kinship Intelligence
  • profits captured by the few
  • costs pushed onto others
  • surveillance · manipulation · disinformation
  • hyperconsumption · waste · externalities
  • members govern what is worth funding
  • surpluses are reinvested
  • harms are reduced and made visible
  • intelligence serves shared missions
How should
intelligence
be used?
From extraction to accountability

3. Everybody Eats

When KI is used, value can be directed back into the people, places, and purposes that matter.

KI Usage
Member-Governed Surplus
pricing · priorities · grants · safeguards
Contributors
the people who do the work
Communities
the places that bear the costs
Shared Missions
care · learning · organizing · creation
Living Systems
restoration · conservation · protection
Build intelligence into the decentralized systems to reduce the need for computation: decision models, less waste, better judgment.
